title: Spiral Matrix
summary: Traverse an m×n matrix in clockwise spiral order from outer perimeter to inner core, returning all elements in a list.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
Write a function to traverse an m×n matrix in spiral order and return all elements in a single list. The traversal should start from the top left corner and proceed clockwise, spiraling inward until every element has been visited.

**Example:**

```
matrix = [
  [0,1,2],
  [3,4,5],
  [6,7,8]
]
```

**Output:** `[0,1,2,5,8,7,6,3,4]`

**Explanation:** The elements are returned in the order they are visited in a clockwise spiral starting from the top left corner.

sections.heading: Key Insight
sections.body: Use a deque to efficiently pop elements from all four directions. Process the matrix in four steps per spiral layer: top row (left to right), right column (top to bottom), bottom row (right to left), and left column (bottom to top). After each layer, the matrix shrinks inward until empty.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
**Top Row:** Pop the first row and extend the result from left to right.

**Right Column:** Traverse the remaining rows and pop the last element of each, appending to result from top to bottom.

**Bottom Row:** Pop the last row and extend the result in reversed order (right to left).

**Left Column:** Traverse the remaining rows in reverse and pop the first element of each, appending from bottom to top.

**Repeat:** Continue spiraling inward until the matrix is empty.

approach: Convert the matrix into a deque of deques for efficient popping from both ends
Pop and extend the top row into result (left to right)
Pop the last element from each remaining row into result (top to bottom)
Pop and extend the bottom row in reversed order into result (right to left)
Pop the first element from each remaining row in reverse order (bottom to top)
Repeat until the matrix is empty

quiz.q: What is the time complexity of the spiral matrix solution?
quiz.explain: We visit every element in the m×n matrix exactly once, so the time complexity is O(m*n).

quiz.q: Why do we check `if matrix and matrix[0]` before traversing columns?
options: To guard against empty rows after popping the top or bottom row
To avoid duplicate elements in the result
To ensure the matrix is square
quiz.explain: After popping the top or bottom row, we may have empty rows remaining. This check ensures we don't try to pop from empty deques.

quiz.q: What happens if we don't reverse the bottom row when extending the result?
options: The spiral order will break, producing elements left-to-right instead of right-to-left
The solution will throw an error
The time complexity increases to O(n²)
Nothing, the result will be the same
quiz.explain: The bottom row must be traversed right-to-left to maintain clockwise spiral order. Without reversing, we'd add elements left-to-right, breaking the pattern.
